desks.Dividends: Microsoft goes ex-dividend Thu Nov 19 at $0.98 per quarter, the first payment at the raised rate (+7.7%) and its 24th consecutive annual increase, payable Dec 10. Apple's $0.27 payment lands Mon Nov 16, but its ex-date (Nov 12) is already past. Nvidia has not yet declared its next ex-date; a December date is expected on pattern but UNVERIFIED. SPY and QQQ December ex-dates are unconfirmed. Tesla pays no dividend.
desks.Earnings: Nvidia is the only watchlist name reporting in the next two weeks, Tue Nov 17 after close, with consensus of $2.49 EPS and about $109 billion in revenue. Options imply a move of about 9.6% (Nov 20 weekly straddle; about 8.6% on the Nov 18 straddle), against a 4.53% average absolute earnings-day move over the last four quarters. Premium into a binary event is to be avoided.
desks.Futures: The EIA weekly petroleum report, released Thu Nov 12 after a Veterans Day delay, showed commercial crude up 4.657 million barrels to 414.4 million, against a draw expected; gasoline rose 1.8 million and distillate 4.1 million. Crude fell about 2.5% for a second straight week (WTI $88.56, Brent $95.84) as the IEA called a fourth-quarter surplus and OPEC+ output rose 1.96 million barrels per day in October. Thursday's 3.3% spike followed unverified Hormuz mine claims that Reuters could not confirm and US Central Command disputed. The November WASDE cut corn ending stocks to 1.758 billion bushels and soybeans to 300 million, both below trade estimates. OPEC+ meets Nov 29.
desks.Parity: No parity violation was found. CBOE launched SPXO, AM-settled SPX weeklies, effective Mon Nov 9: same SPX underlying, price-time allocation instead of pro-rata, and cross-symbol box or conversion legs face execution friction because SPXW cannot leg into the single-leg books with SPX or SPXO. That is the structural item to watch for any future SPX box or conversion construction. No current SPX box-spread rate could be verified from free sources today, so none is quoted.
desks.Premium: All six verdicts are WINDOW-CONTINGENT. The Nov 5 crash day still drives 37-54% of each 20-day realized-variance window, above the 30% threshold, so no clean cheap-or-rich premium verdict is supportable on any name today. Nvidia is the standout: at-the-money implied vol of 92.50% on the Nov 18 expiry, up from 49.06% on the Nov 16 expiry, because Nov 17 earnings sits inside the Nov 18 expiry. That is the event being priced, and premium into it is to be avoided. IV rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names: no free IV-history source is available.
desks.Quant lab: Four new candidates were scored and added to the ledger (#285-288), three WATCH and one ARCHIVE, with no TEST or INTEGRATE movement (top score 51). The sharpest item is #288 (Feng et al): 72% of earnings news appears after the issuer's filing, and the news-reaction association falls to 0.023 from the first trade after publication, a standing caution against any web-news earnings signal. #285 (Gencay) flags an in-loop deflated-Sharpe exploit in autonomous strategy search. All claims are source-reported and UNVERIFIED beyond the abstracts; no code release exists for any WATCH candidate.

items.detail: FRED as of Nov 12: the effective federal funds rate is 3.88%, the 2-year Treasury 4.86% (up 13 basis points since Nov 13), and the 10-year 5.10% (up 12 basis points), putting the 2s10s slope at +24 basis points. The Dec 9 call is unchanged: a 25 basis point hike, 5 HIKE / 1 CUT / 4 NEUTRAL across the ten core indicators, with Kalshi pricing total hike at $0.99 (was $1.00) and the larger-hike tail at $0.11. Waller's Nov 10 trigger for a 50 basis point hike was met by core CPI at +0.3%, giving the tail a named mechanism, though the tail did not grow. At assumed perpetual growth of 3.00%, the Gordon multiple falls to 47.62x from 50.51x, down 5.72%; re-anchor the discount rate to 5.10%.
items.title: Rates: the 10-year rose another 12 bp to 5.10%; the Dec 9 hike call is unchanged

items.detail: The Nov 5 crash day still drives 37-54% of each name's 20-day realized variance, above the 30% threshold, so no clean cheap-or-rich premium verdict is supportable on any name today. Implied vol sits below trailing realized vol on all six names, but that gap is inflated by the crash day in realized. Nvidia's 92.50% at-the-money implied vol on the Nov 18 expiry is an earnings hump, not rich premium. The window un-contaminates only after about Dec 3, when the Nov 5 day exits the 20-day window. IV rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names: no free IV-history source is available.
items.title: Every IV-versus-realized verdict is window-contingent — no clean premium call on any name

items.detail: Crude fell about 2.5% for a second straight week on a surprise EIA build of 4.657 million barrels, the IEA's fourth-quarter surplus call, and OPEC+ supply growth of 1.96 million barrels per day in October. Against that, Thursday brought a 3.3% spike on Hormuz mine claims that Reuters could not confirm and US Central Command disputed, so the move is risk premium, not confirmed supply loss. The curve still says tight now: steep backwardation, with the prompt WTI spread near +$1.05 per barrel. The November WASDE cut corn ending stocks to 1.758 billion bushels and soybeans to 300 million, both well below trade estimates. WTI Dec-26 settled at $88.56; Brent Jan-27 at $95.84.
items.title: Crude fell a second straight week on a surprise build, but the curve still says tight now
